LIVE CAMPAIGN SETUP CONFIRMATION INSTRUCTIONS

Before we begin, you may have most, if not all, of this setup already, so let's systematically work through this by answering the questions below:

  • BEFORE YOU PROCEED: Have you installed the Social Media Magnet plugin on your website?
    1. If Yes - Go to the next question.
    2. If No - Go back and complete "Assignment 2.A-4 Website Setup Instructions" completely, from beginning to end.

Stage 1: Have you input your website URL into your membership profile on the Social Media Magnet website? 

    1. If Yes - Go to the next question.
    2. If No - Proceed to STAGE 1: MEMBERSHIP PROFILE INSTRUCTIONS below, and then return to the next question.

Stage 2: In your Website Analytics --> Settings, have you completed your token authorization process yet and have a GREEN CHECKMARK under the Social Media Magnet Authorization tab?

    1. If Yes - Go to the next question.
    2. If No - Proceed to STAGE 2: TOKEN AUTHORIZATION INSTRUCTIONS in the instruction set below, and then return to the next question.

Stage 3: Website Analytics Google Analytics & Authorization settings at your Website

  • At your Website in your Website Analytics --> Settings, have you connected Google Analytics to our plugin by completing the Google Analytics Authentication process?  When clicking on this tab, you have completed this step if you see a blue "Reset" button.
    1. If Yes - Go to the next question.
    2. If No - Proceed to STAGE 3: GOOGLE ANALYTICS AUTHORIZATION INSTRUCTIONS in the instruction set below, and then return to the next question.

  • At your Website in your Website Analytics --> Settings, have you selected your Live Campaign website from the dropdown button on the Google Analytics Profile Tab? 
      1. If Yes - Go to the next question.
      2. If No - Select your Live Campaign website URL from the dropdown list on your website and make sure you click the blue "Save Changes" button. See steps below STAGE 3: GOOGLE ANALYTICS AUTHORIZATION INSTRUCTIONS

Stage 4: Website Analytics MailChimp settings at your Website

  • At your Website in your Website Analytics --> Settings, have you input all of the required fields for API Key, Username, and List ID under the MailChimp Setting tab?
      1. If Yes, you are completely set up and ready to go for your Live Campaign Start Date.  Congratulations!
      2. If No - Proceed to STAGE 4: MAILCHIMP SETUP INSTRUCTIONS in the instruction set below to complete your Live Campaign Setup Confirmation Instructions.

 

STAGE 1: MEMBERSHIP PROFILE INSTRUCTIONS

Click on the following link to open a different browser window: Open SMM Curriculum.  When this window opens, log in to your SMM curriculum if you are not already logged in. In the right-hand sidebar, click on Membership Details to open your SMM Profile.  Once in your profile, scroll down to Class Info and make sure that all of the following class information is filled out EXACTLY as described below, including the fields for

  1. Company,
  2. Position,
  3. Semester,
  4. Year,
  5. Class Section,
  6. Member ID,
  7. Live Campaign Gmail Email,
  8. Live Campaign Website URL. 

NOTE:  Be sure that you cut and paste the Website URL directly from your website.  In other words, in a separate browser, open up your website.  Then cut the URL out of the search bar and paste it as it appears directly into your "Live Campaign Website URL" field under "Class Info."

 

Lastly, be sure to save your profile after you update it completely.  When you are done, it should resemble the Class Info above. 

NOW RETURN TO Stage #2 at the top of this page.

 

STAGE 2: TOKEN AUTHORIZATION INSTRUCTIONS

Now go back to your WordPress Dashboard and click on the “Website Analytics” tab, and then just underneath it, click on “Settings.”  The first grey tab you will see open is the tab entitled "Social Media Magnet Authorization."  This is where you are going to add your Access Token from your Member Profile page at https://socialmediamagnetpro.com/member-profile/. Next, click on the link to the left to go to your Member Profile page (located under Membership Details on your home screen). Next, scroll down to the Class Info Section, as seen below.

 

First, make sure that your Live Campaign GMail EMail AND your Live Campaign Website URL are correctly listed in your class info.  The Live Campaign Website URL should look EXACTLY like it appears in your web browser when viewing it.  For example, it may OR may NOT have a www. when you view it online.  Now that you have these fields confirmed, you will move onto the Access Token.

At the bottom of the Class Info section, you will see a blue "Regenerate" button next to your Access Token option.  Since you are now setting up your Access Token, click the "Regenerate" button.  This process will create a new token for you that looks like this:

Click the blue "copy & paste" button to the far right of the access token letters.  This will copy the entire token for you to paste into its proper location shortly. 

VERY IMPORTANT STEPS:  First, click the blue "UPDATE" button to confirm your access token.  When you click the update button, the token code will say "Updating..." and then it will disappear, prompting a message that says "Updated Successfully."  Once it has updated successfully, scroll down the page just a bit to a blue button that says "Update Member Profile."  Click this button to save the new token settings into your profile. From this point forward, you NEVER want to "Regenerate" your token again. Otherwise, your Magnet Analytics on your dashboard will NOT report correctly.  You should only do this once during this setup. 

Now that your access token has been copied into your cache, return to the previous browser window (keep this window open) to the Plugin Settings for the Website Analytics Plugin.  As demonstrated below, you will PASTE the previously copied Access Token code into the field labeled "Access Token."  Once it is pasted, click the blue "Save Changes" button.  This should turn the Red X next to the "Access Token" label into a GREEN Checkmark, as seen below. 

Next, at the top of your WordPress dashboard, in a black menu bar that runs horizontally across the page, a menu item called "Managed WordPress."  Now that you have the green checkmark click on the "Managed WordPress" menu item (located just under the address bar in your web browser).  It will create a drop-down menu for the selection called "Flush Cache."  Click on it to flush your website's cache.  After this has been completed, you will see a block box appear with the words, "Success - Cache Cleared."  Close this box. 

Finally, go back to the web browser window open with your member profile. Hit the refresh button on your web browser to refresh the page.  Once the page has been refreshed, you should also see a green checkmark next to the "Access Token" option.  Once again, once this green checkmark appears, NEVER regenerate your access token again.  We want it to stay the same indefinitely from here on out.  Congratulations, you have completed the Access Token Handshake.  Your website access token has now been authenticated! 

NOW RETURN TO Stage #3 at the top of this page.

 

STAGE 3: GOOGLE ANALYTICS AUTHORIZATION INSTRUCTIONS

To authenticate our Google Analytics and connect it to the SMM Plugin, you will need to follow these steps.  First, 1) click on the Website Analytics plugin, then 2) click on the Settings option, and then 3) click on the Google Analytics Authentication tab, as seen below.  If you have not set this up, then you will see a blue link that says: "Click Here to Authenticate," as demonstrated below.

Click on the Click Here to Authenticate link.  After clicking on the "Click here to Authenticate" link, a new window or tab on your browser will open, like the one below, asking you to select the google account to which you want to authenticate.  Choose your newly created BRANDED Gmail account listed in this list of accounts. 

Upon selecting your account, a permission window will open like the one below. Next, you need to hit the "Allow" button, which will permit our SMM Analytics to access your Google account through an API call.

Next, a confirmation screen will open.  Once again, hit the blow "Allow" button in the bottom right-hand corner of the confirmation box.

Next, a window will pop up with your authentication code, as seen below.  Be sure to COPY both lines of text.  We will paste this into the next step.

Once you have copied the code, click back over to your Website Analytics Plugin Settings and paste this code into the data field labeled "Your Access Code:" as seen below.  Be sure to hit the blue "SAVE CHANGES" button to save your new code into the system.

Finally, click the very next tab over, which is the "Google Analytics Profile" tab.  As seen in the screenshot below, you will select your Live Campaign website from the drop-down menu.  Then, be sure to hit the blue "SAVE CHANGES" button to save your Live Campaign website URL into the system.  If you do not hit the save button, your website will NOT be graded. So hit it twice to be sure you saved it!

NOW RETURN TO STAGE #4 at the top of this page.

 

STAGE 4: MAILCHIMP SETUP INSTRUCTIONS

To set up your Mailchimp Setting tab, click on this tab in your Website Analytics Plugin Settings. 

Open up your online MailChimp account in a separate browser that you set up back in the Website Setup Instructions.  (If you haven't created an account yet, you need to go back to the Website Setup Instructions once again and complete all of these instructions first.)  Once you have logged into your online MailChimp account, then follow these steps.

First, click on your name in the upper right-hand corner, and choose Account from the drop-down menu.

In the account menu, click on the “Extras” drop-down menu and select the “API Keys” option.

In the API keys menu, copy your API Key, just like you did in previous steps.

 

Paste this key into your MailChimp Settings tab of the Website Analytics Plugin Settings:

Next, go back to MailChimp, click on your name in the upper right-hand corner, but click on “Profile” this time.  In the Profile screen, copy your username.

Paste your username into your MailChimp Settings tab of the Website Analytics Plugin Settings:

Next, go back to MailChimp, and click on Audience in the Top Menu of your MailChimp FrontPage.  Make sure your actual list (e.g., Audience) is listed in the current audience.  Next, click on the Manage Audience dropdown button to the right.  In this dropdown menu, click on Settings.

Next, in the settings screen, click on “Audience name and defaults.”

On this screen, copy the Audience ID in the right-hand column.  It is in RED letters.  Do NOT copy the "." at the end of your plugin will not function correctly.

 

Next, paste this Red List-ID into your MailChimp Settings "List ID" of the Website Analytics Plugin Settings:

 

CONGRATULATIONS!  You have now completed the Live Campaign Setup Confirmation Instructions.  Your website is mechanically set up and ready to collect data.
title: 7.A-1 Live Campaign Setup Confirmation Instructions

html:
Google Analytics Assignment

Chapter 7 discusses the importance of setting up goal funnels in Google Analytics.  If you have completed your Website Setup Instructions, you have already completed setting up one destination goal funnel for your Email Registration through MailChimp.  Since this one is so important, we helped you with this one. However, if you don't remember what this did, it tracked users from one URL destination (i.e., your email registration form) to another URL destination (i.e., your email registration thank you page). This Google tracking process helps you determine if users are bouncing off of your form in the real world.  When identified, it will help you strategize why this might be the case so that you can correct this issue when your form completion percentage is low. Therefore, using analytics to track these goal funnels are essential.

Another goal funnel that we helped you set up was the "destination goal" in Google Analytics associated with your "Contact Us" form.  Again, the goal tracked users from the form submission page to the thank you page. Now it's time to add two more destination goals, just like the previous Contact Us form, using Ninja Forms. 

Remember, for each destination goal that you will set up for this assignment. You will need first to create the survey in Ninja Forms that will collect the data from each individual. For example, if you were doing a music blog and had a Spotify channel, you may want to ask your readers to request a song on the channel. Therefore, you would set up a ninja form for the reader to complete to request the song. Once the form was submitted, the ninja form would alert you of the song request and email the reader alerting them that the request was submitted. The form would then redirect the reader to the thank you page. Like with the contact-us form, part of this process is to track the goal funnel as the reader moves from the submission page to the thank you page by setting up another destination goal within Google Analytics. Again, all of this replicates the contact us form previously created in your Website Setup Instructions. Go back to this instruction set for the step-by-step instructions of this process.

Therefore, this assignment aims to create TWO new goal funnels that are specifically targeted towards those readers who have already joined the email subscription list. You don’t want them to sign up and then have nothing else to do during the length of your practicum campaign. Content in your weekly email should be directed at your loyal readers who have already joined the email subscription list to move them back to the website where they can complete these two new goal funnels. This keeps the magnet mechanism working, moving new readers through the contact us and follow-me goals while also moving loyal customers back to the website, increasing customer retention through these two new goals. You would have more than two in the real world, but for the eight-week campaign, two is enough. If you have more than two ideas, you are welcome to create more goal funnels beyond just these extra two, but I would only do up to three or four to not muddy the messaging for all of the different goals. For this assignment, only two are required.
 
As we said in your Website Setup Instructions, there are a lot of different options here.  Think strategically about these goals and what they will mean to the customer experience.  After setting them BOTH up, you will need to complete your assignment by writing a one-page memo about the two goals you created.  This is a one-page total, so a half-page of the rationale for each goal.  Please discuss why you chose these goals, what you expect them to accomplish, and how you can use the data to enhance the customer experience on your site. 
 

FOR COURSE CREDIT:  This assignment memo should be single-spaced, size 12 Times New Roman, Arial, Calibri, or Cambria font with 1-inch margins.  Do NOT double space!
title: 7.A-2 Google Analytics Assignment

html:
Progress Reports

At the end of Chapter 7, we discussed your website analytics features from The Social Media Magnet Dashboard.  We descriptively went through each analytic segment that is collected by our Magnet Analytics software and demonstrated how these metrics were assessed (graded) and how those assessments (grades) were arranged into categorical elements (Brand Awareness, Brand Acquisition, and Brand Retention) to help you assess your own campaign. Again, this assessment of your own campaign occurs as you examine your performance for each category or individual metric (users, new users, page views, etc.).  Remember that your individual performance across each metric or category is benchmarked against our population's mean and standard deviation of actual campaigns.  Therefore, if you have a performance grade reported as 80, then you are right on the mean.  A 70 is one standard deviation below the mean, while 90 is above the mean.  Hence, if you are sitting at an 80, you know you have room to grow your success in this benchmark.  The purpose of this progress report is to evaluate your strengths and weaknesses using your Magnet Analytics progress as the benchmark.  Then it would be best if you examined other campaigns you may be aware of to see how you might be able to identify opportunities where you can improve your weaknesses and defend your strengths from the threat of other competitors improving their weaknesses.

Therefore, for this progress report, one of three that you will complete during your Live Campaign, we want you to conduct a SWOT Analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) for this self-assessment.  That is, we want you to describe the internal Strengths and Weaknesses that your campaign currently exhibits using your performance metrics reported within your Magnet Analytics.  Then we want you to discuss the external Opportunities and threats you perceive to exist by conducting an external analysis of other campaigns and competitors in your market.  Conducting these SWOT analyses will prepare you for your Final Report, including a final SWOT.

This progress report should be 1-2 pages, single-spaced, size 12 Times New Roman, Arial, Calibri, or Cambria font with 1-inch margins.  Do NOT double space, and do not type less than one page.  These progress reports are valuable because you will learn how to assess your performance honestly.
title: 10.A-2 Progress Reports

html:
Email Analysis Assignment

Using the reporting functions of MailChimp, give an overview of the entire email campaign.  What has worked for you?  What hasn’t worked for you?  Discuss your best email to date and why you believe it was successful.  Discuss your worst email to date and why you think it wasn’t successful.  In this particular discussion, highlight any seasonality or anomalies that may have been present.  Finally, in the last paragraph, discuss a potential A/B test that you could run to test something about your email strategy.  What would you run and why?

This assignment memo should be single-spaced, size 12 Times New Roman, Arial, Calibri, or Cambria font with 1-inch margins.
title: 13.A1 Email Analysis Assignment

html:
Closing-the-Loop Assignment

This assignment is an extension of the Campaign Congruency Exercise.  This assignment aims to have a group of family, friends, coworkers, etc., each independently evaluate your campaign and provide you feedback. We recommend six to ten individuals provide you feedback to you, and then you are to complete the Closing the Loop memo.  In this memo, you are to write the findings and feedback related to your project in this format:

Paragraph #1:  You need to explain what similarities or differences exist in your hub-and-spoke design, per your group’s feedback.  Be sure to speak to its level of congruent or incongruent messaging. Did they get the message and brand focus you desire to convey?

Paragraph #2:  Explain why you think they would have perceived your messaging in this way.  Remember, perception is reality.  If you see consensus in their evaluation, then this is truly your message, whether it was intended or not. Was this the message you intended for them to have?

Paragraph #3:  Explain your primary narrative again.  Remember back to your original narrative exercise. Have you strayed off the narrative?  If so, why? In other words, explain how your perceived message is different than your intended message.  If you haven’t strayed off the narrative, and it is the same, then explain how you have made a concerted effort to stay on narrative.  Has this been easy or difficult?

Paragraph #4:  What top three recommendations do you need to make to get back on narrative, or at least tighten up your narrative.  Remember the importance of your narrative at the beginning of the project. The narrative exercise is the most important assignment of the project.  Brands that can’t stay on narrative don’t succeed.  These recommendations are critical for the final push on your project.  Think long and hard about the three recommendations, and then outline how you plan to implement them in this paragraph, indicating WHAT they are and HOW you will implement these three strategies moving forward.

This is your final memo and is VERY important; therefore, it should be no less than TWO-typed pages in length.  It should be single-spaced, size 12 Times New Roman, Arial, Calibri, or Cambria font with 1-inch margins.
title: 14.A1 Closing-the-Loop Assignment

html:
Social Media Magnet Pro Final Report and Plan Instructions – PowerPoint Report

Directions:  Your final project is to create a report & plan in a PowerPoint presentation regarding your brand, social media campaign, and calendar. The goal of this final report is to create a compendium of what you have developed for your brand, learned about social media, and provide some insight into real takeaways from your experience to provide the roadmap into the future. This will be your blueprint and guide to refer back to, share with your team and review every six to twelve months to tenure you are on track for success.

Final Report – Your Plan

  • Create a Final Report and Plan PDF
  • Add your Brand Story: story, beliefs, promises, and trust
  • Provide Screenshots of your website
  • Include slides with your Brand Overview, Message Matrix, Interactions & Initial Calendar
  • SWOT Analysis
  • The Notes you created during the process
  • Analytics Results
  • Action Items Moving Forward

First, please reflect on why you signed up for this course and what you expected to learn.  Then provide your opinion on whether you met that goal describing why or why not you met this objective.  In other words, it is ok to be a little critical of any certain area of the course and Live Campaign that you thought would be different than expected.

Next, you are to perform a SWOT analysis of your social media campaign.  What internal strengths and weaknesses did you possess and why?  What external opportunities did you exploit, and what external threats could you not overcome?  Please use your competition for the external analysis.  In other words, how does your competition measure up when compared to your own campaign.  This will require you to do some external research on their websites, blogs, and social media pages, as you compare your final product.  Measure and evaluate your campaign performance using your Magnet Analytics.

Finally, you need to explain why you believe your campaign was successful.  What drove success for you?  Which social media channels were best, and why?  What type of blog post worked and why?  What were your Google and MailChimp stats?  Did you set goals for yourself, and did you meet those goals?  What is the biggest takeaway from your Live Campaign?  Remember that you need to include all of your social media analytics here to be able to measure success.  Please include your Social Media Magnet Comparisons (You vs. Campaign Average Stats) and your Brand Story, Calendar, visual depiction of your Brand Awareness, Brand Acquisition, and your Brand Retention metrics. (NOTE: You can access these three specifically from your Magnet Analytics.).  Don’t forget this part, it is very important! 

As to the format, it is completely open to your own design.  We don’t want to limit your possibilities, so make it professional and unique to you.  This project is to capture the work you did and document your plan moving forward. If you submit it to us BY EMAIL, we will evaluate it and review it. 

Finally, a PDF sample is included below as a “Final Report & Plan Example.” Please use this as a starting point, NOT a template.  Please make your presentation unique to your campaign and you.  DON’T COPY THIS SAMPLE REPORT. However, note, your submission should NOT be in PDF format but should be in PowerPoint format so that we can read the NOTES section of your PowerPoint PPT file. 

The notes you add to your sldies are critical to the content portion of your report and plan as you need to include your explanations for each slide in the notes section of the slide (like you would be presenting it to your executive team or board of directors).  While the slides should include these topics, the explanation of each topic should be included in the notes section. Your presentation should be balanced on 50% style of the presentation (i.e., what each slide looks like) and 50% content (i.e., how you explain yourself within the notes sections).

Download Final Report & Plan Example (for style only, no notes are included in this presentation)
